chunks: 2962 - And he, peace be upon him, said regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"So travel freely throughout the land for four months."

He said: "They are twenty days of Dhu al-Hijjah, al-Muharram, Safar, the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, and ten days from the month of Rabi' al-Akhir; and the ten days from the beginning of Dhu al-Hijjah are not counted within the four months."

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ: the four-month period being explained and calculated
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the land or earth in which movement is permitted during the appointed time
key_terms.الْمُحَرَّمَ: Muharram, one of the months included in the count
key_terms.ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: Dhu al-Hijjah, the month from which part of the calculation begins
key_terms.رَبِيعٍ الْآخِرِ: Rabi' al-Akhir, from which ten days complete the four-month period
key_terms.رَبِيعٍ الْأَوَّلِ: Rabi' al-Awwal, one of the months included in the count
key_terms.صَفَرَ: Safar, one of the months included in the count
key_terms.فَسِيحُوا: move freely or travel in the land without restriction for the stated period

ai.seo_question: How did Imam عليه السلام explain the four sacred months mentioned in Qur'an 9:2?
ai.summary: The Imam عليه السلام explains the Qur'anic phrase about four months by specifying their exact span, beginning from twenty days of Dhu al-Hijjah and extending through ten days of Rabi' al-Akhir. This report clarifies how the four-month period is calculated and indicates that the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah are excluded from that count.
